note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in KY.json, gathered 2026-10-04 (the KYTC list, FHWA, NPS, byway organizations and Wikipedia).

byways.name: Abraham Lincoln Heritage Highway
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (part of Lincoln Heritage Scenic Highway)
byways.where: US 150 between Bardstown, Springfield, Perryville and Danville; Nelson, Washington, Boyle counties; 34 mi

facts.fact: The Lincoln Heritage Scenic Highway is a 71.2-mile National Scenic Byway through the knobs from Hodgenville via Bardstown, Springfield and Perryville to Danville.
The Mordecai Lincoln House, six miles north of Springfield, was the home of Abraham Lincoln's uncle and is the only house owned by a Lincoln family member still standing in Kentucky.
The Battle of Perryville was fought on October 8, 1862; the 745-acre state historic site has monuments, cannons and an interpretive museum.

byways.name: Big Bone Lick/Middle Creek Parkway
byways.where: KY 338, KY 2852, KY 536 and KY 18 from US 42 at Beaverlick to Woolper Road at Commissary Corner; Boone County; 19.9 mi

facts.fact: Mammoths are believed to have been drawn to Big Bone Lick by a salt lick deposited around its sulfur springs; mastodon, bison and ground sloth fossils have also been found.
Meriwether Lewis visited Big Bone Lick in late 1803 to collect bones, and William Clark removed over 300 bones there in 1807.
The parkway follows KY 338, KY 2852, KY 536 and KY 18 from US 42 at Beaverlick to Woolper Road at Commissary Corner, 19.931 miles, designated 5/24/1995.

byways.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (Bill Monroe Bluegrass Trail)
byways.where: US 62, KY 69, US 231, KY 1544, KY 54, US 60, KY 56 and others via Rosine, Hartford, Fordsville, Hawesville, Lewisport, Owensboro; Ohio, Hancock, Daviess counties; 113.8 mi (plus a 2007 US 231 extension in Ohio County)

facts.fact: Bill Monroe was born on his family's farm near Rosine and is buried in the Rosine Cemetery.
From April to mid-December, musicians gather in Rosine on Friday nights to play bluegrass in the small general store and in the barn next to it.
Owensboro is home to the Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame and Museum.

byways.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (Everly Brothers Rock-N-Roll Trail)
byways.where: KY 56, US 41A, KY 132, KY 136, KY 81, US 431, KY 176, KY 189 and US 62 via Sebree, Calhoun, Central City; Webster, McLean, Muhlenberg counties; 99.9 mi

facts.fact: Don Everly was born in Brownie, Muhlenberg County, on February 1, 1937.
Brownie was an unincorporated community that eventually became part of Central City.
Central City began hosting an Everly Brothers Homecoming on Labor Day weekend in 1988.

byways.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (W.C. Handy Blues Trail)
byways.where: US 60, US 41A and KY 56 from Owensboro west via Henderson, Corydon and Morganfield to the Webster County line; Daviess, Henderson, Union counties; 59.5 mi

facts.fact: W. C. Handy met his wife Elizabeth Price while performing at a barbecue in Henderson in 1896.
Henderson grew from a village called Red Banks, named for the reddish clay of its bluffs over the Ohio River, and holds a Handy Blues and Barbecue Festival each June.
The trail follows US 60 and US 41A from Owensboro via Henderson and Corydon to Morganfield, then KY 56 south, 59.525 miles, designated 1/29/2004.

byways.name: Boone Creek Scenic Byway
byways.where: KY 418, Grimes Mill Road and McCalls Mill Road loop near Athens; Fayette and Clark counties; 8.6 mi

facts.fact: The Grimes Mill on Boone's Creek, built in 1803, is a two-and-a-half-story building with quarried-stone walls three and a half feet thick, in use as a mill until 1927.
The Iroquois Hunt Club bought Grimes Mill in 1928 and uses it as its headquarters.
The byway loops from KY 418 near Athens via Grimes Mill Road and McCalls Mill Road in Fayette and Clark counties, 8.6 miles, designated 5/24/1995.

byways.name: Cordell Hull Highway
byways.where: KY 255, KY 70, KY 90, US 31E, US 68, KY 63, KY 100 and KY 163 from Mammoth Cave National Park via Glasgow to the Tennessee line; Barren and Monroe counties; 51.6 mi

facts.fact: The byway begins at the entrance to Mammoth Cave National Park, runs to Glasgow and ends at the Tennessee border on KY 63; the Old Mulkey Meetinghouse State Historic Site lies near the Tennessee border.
Old Mulkey Meetinghouse, built in 1804, is the oldest log meetinghouse in Kentucky, has twelve corners in the shape of a cross, and Daniel Boone's sister Hannah is buried in its cemetery.
Glasgow is known for its annual Scottish Highland Games.

byways.name: Country Music Highway
byways.where: US 23 (with US 119 near Jenkins) from the Virginia line via Pikeville, Prestonsburg, Paintsville, Louisa, Ashland to Greenup; Letcher, Pike, Floyd, Johnson, Lawrence, Boyd, Greenup counties; 144.1 mi

facts.fact: A 1994 act of the Kentucky General Assembly named US 23 'The Country Music Highway', and a sign at each county line lists the country music stars from that county.
Loretta Lynn was born in Butcher Hollow, a coal-mining community near Van Lear in Johnson County, and sang of it in 'Coal Miner's Daughter'.
The U.S. 23 Country Music Highway Museum in Paintsville profiles entertainers who grew up near the highway, including Loretta Lynn, Crystal Gayle and Hylo Brown.

byways.name: Cumberland Cultural Heritage Highway
byways.where: KY 90, KY 163, US 68, KY 80, KY 61, KY 55, US 127, US 150 and KY 78 linking Burkesville, Albany, Monticello, Cumberland Falls, Edmonton, Columbia, Campbellsville, Greensburg, Russell Springs, Liberty, Danville, Stanford; 13 counties; 187.2 mi

facts.fact: The 187.2-mile byway has several sections, including KY 90 from Burkesville to Monticello around Lake Cumberland and routes from Columbia toward Campbellsville and Danville with a loop to Stanford.
The KY 90 section ends at the entrance to the DuPont Lodge at Cumberland Falls State Resort Park.
Cumberland Falls is 68 feet tall and one of the few places in the western hemisphere where a moonbow can often be seen on full-moon nights.

byways.name: Duncan Hines Scenic Tour
byways.where: Loop from Bowling Green via KY 101, KY 259, KY 70, Brownsville, Bee Spring and through Mammoth Cave National Park by the Green River Ferry, returning via Smiths Grove and Oakland; Warren and Edmonson counties; 83 mi

facts.fact: Duncan Hines, born in Bowling Green, published the restaurant guide Adventures in Good Eating in 1935.
The Green River Ferry is the only active river ferry in Mammoth Cave National Park, carrying vehicles, hikers and bikers across the Green River.
The 83-mile tour begins at Duncan Hines's former home on US 31W in Bowling Green and crosses Mammoth Cave National Park by the Green River Ferry.

byways.name: Great River Road
byways.where: KY 94, KY 239, KY 123, KY 58, KY 80, KY 1203 and US 51 from the Tennessee line via Hickman, Columbus and Wickliffe to the Ohio River bridge; Fulton, Hickman, Carlisle, Ballard counties

facts.fact: FHWA lists the Kentucky section of the Great River Road as an All-American Road.
At Columbus-Belmont State Park a Confederate chain once stretched across the Mississippi to Belmont, Missouri; its links were eleven inches long and its anchor weighed four to six tons.
Wickliffe Mounds is a Mississippian-culture archaeological site outside Wickliffe, about 3 miles from the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi rivers.

byways.name: Highway 524 Loop
byways.where: KY 524 loop off US 42 between Goshen and Sligo through Westport; Oldham County

facts.fact: The KY 524 loop leaves and rejoins the US 42 scenic byway between Goshen and Sligo, passing through Westport, designated 2/24/2011.
Westport is a small Oldham County community on the Ohio River whose post office opened in 1815.

byways.name: Hughes Lane
byways.where: Hughes Lane from KY 353 (Russell Cave Road) to US 27/68 (Paris Pike); Fayette County; 2.2 mi

facts.fact: Hughes Lane runs 2.220 miles from KY 353 (Russell Cave Road) to US 27/68 (Paris Pike), designated 11/20/1996.
When Paris Pike was rebuilt, its dry-laid limestone rock fences were taken down and rebuilt by hand; the project won a 2002 design award.

byways.name: Ironworks Pike
byways.where: KY 1973 from US 27/68 (Paris Pike) to I-75 exit 120; Fayette County; 7.2 mi

facts.fact: KY 1973 follows Iron Works Pike from US 27/68, crossing Russell Cave Road and Newtown Pike, past horse farms and the Kentucky Horse Park before reaching I-75.
The 1,224-acre Kentucky Horse Park, opened in 1978 at I-75 exit 120 off Iron Works Pike, has a statue of Man o' War over his grave near the entrance.

byways.name: KY 160-Black Mountain
byways.where: KY 160 from Looney Creek at Benham through Lynch up Black Mountain to the Virginia line; Harlan County; 10.3 mi

facts.fact: Black Mountain, at 4,145 feet, is the highest point in Kentucky, rising just above the towns of Lynch and Appalachia, Virginia.
Lynch was laid out in 1917 by a U.S. Steel subsidiary as a company coal town and had 10,000 people by the 1940s.
Benham, in the valley of Looney Creek, began as an International Harvester company town and is a National Register historic district.

byways.name: KY 89
byways.where: KY 89 and US 421 from KY 490 in Rockcastle County via McKee to the Estill County line; Rockcastle and Jackson counties; 35.5 mi

facts.fact: The route follows KY 89 and US 421 from KY 490 in Rockcastle County via McKee to the Estill County line, 35.517 miles, designated 11/20/1996.
McKee, founded in 1882, is the county seat and only city in Jackson County, and lies within the Daniel Boone National Forest.

byways.name: Mary Ingles Highway
byways.where: KY 8 through Augusta; Bracken County

facts.fact: KY 8 is named the Mary Ingles Highway for part of its length, after Mary Draper Ingles, who escaped a Shawnee salt-making party at Big Bone Lick and crossed the Kentucky wilderness home to Virginia.
Mary Draper Ingles was captured in 1755 and walked 500 to 600 miles home after escaping.
In Augusta, KY 8 is Fifth Street, and the Augusta Ferry crosses the Ohio River to Brown County, Ohio.

byways.name: North Cleveland Road
byways.where: KY 1973 (North Cleveland Road) from KY 418 at Athens to US 60 (Winchester Road); Fayette County

facts.fact: The byway connects KY 418 (Athens-Boonesboro Road) with US 60 (Winchester Road), designated 12/15/2008.
Athens, first settled in 1786 as Cross Plains and chartered in 1826, has a National Register historic district of Italianate, Greek Revival and Victorian buildings.

byways.name: Old Frankfort Pike
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (Old Frankfort Pike Historic and Scenic Byway)
byways.where: KY 1681 from Wolf Run Creek in Lexington to Duckers Station Road in Woodford County; Fayette and Woodford counties; 14.5 mi

facts.fact: The 15.5-mile designated byway has a canopy of hardwood trees and miles of dry-laid limestone rock fences, and passes through six National Register rural historic districts.
KY 1681 passes the site of Woodburn Stud, called the birthplace of Kentucky's thoroughbred industry, now operated as Airdrie Stud.
FHWA lists Old Frankfort Pike Historic and Scenic Byway as a National Scenic Byway, describing traditional diversified farming alongside the equine industry.

byways.name: Old Kentucky Turnpike
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (part of Lincoln Heritage Scenic Highway)
byways.where: US 31E from the Abraham Lincoln Birthplace via Hodgenville to Bardstown, then US 62/US 150 to My Old Kentucky Home State Park; Larue and Nelson counties; 28.1 mi

facts.fact: Lincoln was born on February 12, 1809, in a one-room log cabin at Sinking Spring Farm south of Hodgenville; a symbolic cabin is kept inside a 1911 neoclassical memorial building.
My Old Kentucky Home State Park in Bardstown centers on Federal Hill, the home of Senator John Rowan, associated with Stephen Foster's song 'My Old Kentucky Home, Good Night'.
The route runs on US 31E from the Lincoln birthplace via Hodgenville to Bardstown, 28.059 miles, designated 5/24/1995.

byways.name: Old Richmond Road (US25)/Grimes Mill Road
byways.where: From KY 418 near Jacobson Park across I-75 via Grimes Mill Road to McCalls Mill Road; Fayette County; 6.8 mi

facts.fact: The route runs from KY 418 near Jacobson Park across I-75 via Grimes Mill Road to McCalls Mill Road, 6.8 miles, designated 10/6/1999.

The Grimes House and Mill Complex on Boone's Creek includes the mill, the Grimes family home, a quarried-stone springhouse beside Grimes Mill Road, a cemetery and the ruins of a flax house and a distillery.

byways.name: Pine Mountain Road
byways.where: US 119 from KY 15 in Whitesburg to KY 806 near Oven Fork; Letcher County; 8.2 mi

facts.fact: The 8.15-mile byway crosses Pine Mountain and the Little Shepherd Trail on US 119 from Whitesburg to Oven Fork.
Pine Mountain is a ridge about 125 miles long; only two waterways, the Cumberland River at Pineville and the Clear Fork near Jellico, cut through it.
US 119 crosses Pine Mountain south of Whitesburg.

byways.name: Pisgah Pike
byways.where: KY 1967 from 0.5 mi north of US 60 to KY 1681 (Old Frankfort Pike); Woodford County; 5.1 mi

facts.fact: The byway is 5.07 miles long between Versailles and Lexington, passing The Kentucky Castle, with Keeneland further east.
Pisgah was settled in 1784 by a colony from Virginia; Pisgah Presbyterian Church was founded in 1784 and its present building dates from 1812.

byways.name: Red River Gorge Scenic Byways
byways.where: KY 11, KY 77 (Nada Tunnel), KY 715 and KY 15 loop from Stanton via Nada, Pine Ridge and Slade to the Lee County line; Powell, Menifee, Wolfe counties; 45 mi

facts.fact: The Red River Gorge Geological Area in the Daniel Boone National Forest has more than 100 natural sandstone arches.
Nada Tunnel on KY 77 is a 900-foot former logging-railroad tunnel blasted through sandstone in 1910-1911, now paved for a single lane of traffic.
The byway is 46 miles long; FHWA suggests an hour to drive it or five hours to see it.

byways.name: Ridgetop Scenic Byway (KY 89)
byways.where: KY 89 across Estill County from the Jackson County line to the Clark County line

facts.fact: The byway follows KY 89 across Estill County from the Jackson County line to the Clark County line, designated 10/1/2013.
Irvine and Ravenna sit along the Kentucky River in central Estill County; iron smelting began in the county in 1810, and the ruins of the Estill, Cottage and Fitchburg furnaces are still visible.

byways.name: River Road
byways.where: River Road in Louisville from US 42 near Prospect to Zorn Avenue; Jefferson County; 7 mi

facts.fact: The byway follows River Road 7 miles from US 42 near Prospect to Zorn Avenue in Louisville, designated 5/24/1995.
The Louisville Water Tower, at Zorn Avenue and River Road, began operating in 1860; its 183-foot Doric column rises from a Corinthian portico on a hill overlooking the Ohio River.

byways.name: Riverboat Row
byways.where: Riverboat Row in Newport from KY 8 to James Taylor City Park; Campbell County; 1 mi

facts.fact: The one-mile byway runs along the Ohio River from Newport to James Taylor City Park, past floating restaurants and riverboats, near the Newport Southbank (Purple People) Bridge to Cincinnati.
It begins at KY 8 (Dave Cowens Drive) in Newport, 1 mile, designated 5/24/1995.

byways.name: Russell Cave Road
byways.where: KY 353 from KY 1973 (Ironworks Pike) to Hughes Lane; Fayette County; 2.5 mi

facts.fact: The designated section runs 2.461 miles on KY 353 from KY 1973 (Ironworks Pike) to Hughes Lane, designated 11/20/1996.
KY 353 (Russell Cave Road) runs from New Circle Road in Lexington northeast toward Bourbon and Harrison counties, crossing North Elkhorn Creek.
Iron Works Pike, which meets Russell Cave Road at the start of the section, passes horse farms on its way to the Kentucky Horse Park.

byways.name: Shakertown Road
byways.where: US 68 for 1.2 mi either side of the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill entrance; Mercer County; 2.4 mi

facts.fact: The byway runs 2.4 miles on US 68 into Shakertown, described as the most completely restored Shaker community in the nation, past long runs of hand-laid stone fence.
Pleasant Hill was home to a Shaker community from 1805 to 1910; by 1825 it had large stone and brick dwellings, grassy lawns and stone sidewalks.

byways.name: The Zollicoffer-Thomas Scenic Byway (KY 235 Mill Springs Battlefield)
byways.where: KY 235 from KY 80 at Nancy, then Old Mill Springs Battlefield Road to the Ferry Landing tour stop; Pulaski and Wayne counties; 10.4 mi

facts.fact: At the Battle of Mill Springs in January 1862, Union troops under George H. Thomas met Confederates at Logan's Crossroads and Confederate general Felix Zollicoffer was killed.

The battlefield became a national monument, established as a National Park Service unit on September 22, 2020; Logan's Crossing is now the town of Nancy, where the visitor center stands beside Mill Springs National Cemetery.
The byway follows KY 235 from KY 80 at Nancy and Old Mill Springs Battlefield Road to the Ferry Landing tour stop, 10.36 miles, designated 9/11/2001.

byways.name: US 42
byways.where: US 42 from Goshen Lane in Goshen to KY 3223; Oldham County; 14.8 mi

facts.fact: The byway follows US 42 for 14.8 miles from Goshen Lane in Goshen to KY 3223, with a small loop near the Ohio River and access to Hermitage Farm, where visitors can see horses.
The KY 524 loop off this byway passes through Westport, a riverside community whose post office opened in 1815.

byways.name: US 62-Midway-Versailles Road
byways.where: US 62 from Parrish Avenue in Midway to US 60 in Versailles; Woodford County; 6.3 mi

facts.fact: Horse farms including Fawn Leap, Shadowlawn, Adena Springs and Stonewall lie along US 62 between Parrish Avenue in Midway and US 60 in Versailles.
Midway was founded in 1835 by the Lexington and Ohio Railroad as Kentucky's first railroad town, named for its location between Lexington and Frankfort.

byways.name: US 68
byways.where: US 68 in three segments, Lebanon via Perryville and Harrodsburg to Jessamine County, Lexington via Paris to Nicholas County, and the Licking River to Maysville and the Ohio line; 11 counties; 103.8 mi

facts.fact: The byway follows a historic path once used by buffalo and later an 1800s Shaker road, past black and white plank fences, horse barns, tobacco fields and limestone rock fences.
Blue Licks Battlefield State Resort Park, near Mount Olivet on US 68, marks the August 19, 1782 Battle of Blue Licks at salt springs where buffalo herds once gathered.
Washington, founded in 1786 and now part of Maysville, is where Harriet Beecher Stowe witnessed a slave auction.

byways.name: US Highway 68
byways.where: US 68 connecting Lebanon and Paducah via Bowling Green, Russellville, Hopkinsville and Cadiz; Marion to McCracken counties

facts.fact: US 68 passes Bowling Green, Russellville, Hopkinsville and Cadiz; the Jefferson Davis State Historic Site at Fairview, about 9 miles east of Hopkinsville, is along the highway.
The Jefferson Davis monument at Fairview is a 351-foot concrete obelisk marking Davis's birthplace.
An annual 400-mile yard sale is held along US 68 for four days in early summer.

byways.name: Van Meter, Rice, and Elkchester Roads
byways.where: Van Meter Road and KY 1969 (Rice and Elkchester roads) between US 60 (Versailles Road) and KY 1681 (Old Frankfort Pike); Fayette County; 6.3 mi

facts.fact: The route runs on Van Meter Road and KY 1969 (Rice and Elkchester roads) between US 60 (Versailles Road) and KY 1681 (Old Frankfort Pike), 6.295 miles, designated 11/20/1996.
Keeneland Race Course is at 4201 Versailles Road in Lexington.
Old Frankfort Pike is lined with miles of dry-laid limestone rock fences.

byways.name: Wilderness Road Heritage Highway
byways.where: US 25E from KY 441 near Middlesboro to Barbourville area, then US 25 from London via Mount Vernon to Berea; Bell, Knox, Laurel, Rockcastle, Madison counties; 93.8 mi

facts.fact: In March 1775 the Transylvania Company hired Daniel Boone to blaze a trail through the Cumberland Gap; modern highways follow much of the Wilderness Road's route.
The Renfro Valley Barn Dance, founded by John Lair in 1939, gave early stage time to Hank Williams and Red Foley and was broadcast on CBS Radio until the late 1950s.
FHWA describes the 93.8-mile byway as leading to Cumberland Gap, Renfro Valley and Berea, which it calls Kentucky's crafts capital.

byways.name: Winchester Road Corridor
byways.where: US 60 (Winchester Road) from the Lexington urban service boundary to the Clark County line; Fayette County; 4.8 mi

facts.fact: The corridor runs 4.8 miles on US 60 from the Lexington Urban Service Area boundary to the Clark County line, designated 2/24/2011.
In 1958 Lexington enacted the nation's first urban growth boundary, restricting new development to an urban service area to keep open land around its horse farms.

byways.name: Woodlands Trace
byways.where: The Trace through Land Between the Lakes from the Lake Barkley-Kentucky Lake canal to the Tennessee line; Lyon and Trigg counties; 30 mi in Kentucky

facts.fact: Woodlands Trace runs 43 miles along a ridge between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley through Land Between the Lakes.
Elk and bison roam free in a 700-acre tallgrass prairie enclosure at Golden Pond, seen from a 3.5-mile paved loop road.
The Tennessee portion of the road was renamed 'The Trace', short for 'Buffalo Trace', after paths that followed the seasonal migrations of bison.
